name: Canada Critical Cyber Systems Protection Act
summary: Canada's Critical Cyber Systems Protection Act (CCSPA) establishes a cybersecurity framework for designated operators of federally regulated critical infrastructure. It was enacted by Bill C-8 (S.C. 2026, c. 9), which received Royal Assent on 15 June 2026, after its predecessor Bill C-26 died when Parliament was prorogued in January 2025. The Act comes into force on dates fixed by order of the Governor in Council, and no such order had been made as of October 2026, so it is not yet in force and no operator classes have been designated. Not to be confused with the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act (CCPSA).
keyRequirements: Designated operators must establish a cybersecurity program within 90 days of designation, file it with their regulator, and review it annually
Identify and mitigate cybersecurity risks in the supply chain and from third-party products and services
Report cybersecurity incidents to the Communications Security Establishment within the prescribed period, not exceeding 72 hours, and notify the regulator
Comply with cybersecurity directions issued by the Governor in Council
Keep records of the cybersecurity program, incidents, supply-chain mitigation, and directions in Canada
Covers federally regulated sectors: telecommunications, finance, energy, and transportation
penalties: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 per violation for individuals and CAD 15 million for any other person. Offences carry fines at the court's discretion and, for individuals convicted on indictment, up to 5 years imprisonment; each day of a continuing violation is a separate offence. Compliance orders and injunctions.
